name: Beracah
overview: Beracah was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the Anathothite. He is noted for coming to David at Ziklag, indicating his allegiance during a significant period in David's life. His tribal affiliation and unique designation highlight his place within the community during the early monarchy.
namesAndTitles: The name Beracah means "blessing," reflecting a positive and meaningful designation. This proper name is noted in 1 Chronicles 12:3, though it was not given directly by God. The meaning of his name aligns with the biblical theme of God's blessings on His people.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Beracah as a descendant of Benjamin, situating him within this tribe. Beyond this tribal relationship, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Beracah's significance lies in his identity as an Anathothite from Benjamin who joined David at Ziklag, demonstrating the gathering of support for David among the tribes. His presence among those who came to David reflects the consolidation of David's leadership and the fulfillment of God's plan for his kingship. Beracah represents the faithful remnant within Benjamin who aligned with God's anointed.
